title: Core Competencies
equation: Strategic Range = Core Competence × Adjacent Market Reach
hook: Being okay at a lot of things won't build a company. Being rare at one thing might.
statement: Build your strategy on strengths that are rare, hard to copy, and useful across more than one market.
explainer: One company's engine know-how powered motorcycles, cars, lawn mowers and generators. A deep root lets you grow into new markets. Expanding just because the money looks good usually flops.
sop: List everything your business is good at.
Keep only what's rare, lasting, and useful in other markets.
Pick your top 1 to 3 as your core.
Point hiring and investment at deepening them.
Use them to step into nearby markets.
equation_example: Score each 1 to 10. Core Competence 8, Adjacent Market Reach 6. 8 × 6 = 48 out of 100. Higher means one deep skill could carry you into new products or markets. Lower means your strength is too narrow or shallow to stretch.
question: Name the one thing your business does that would be really hard for anyone else to copy.
closing_statement: One deep root can grow many branches.
caption:
Principle Nº 283: Core Competencies

Being okay at a lot of things won't build a company. Being rare at one thing might.

Build your strategy on strengths that are rare, hard to copy, and useful across more than one market.
